ef-01-bencaos.context: Paul writes to the saints in Ephesus and, before teaching, opens with praise. He looks at what God has already done in Christ, since before the foundation of the world.
ef-01-bencaos.focusQuestion: Which blessing in Christ do you need to remember today before asking for something new?
ef-01-bencaos.keywordGloss: Everything God gives his people comes through Christ, not through our merit.
facts: God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ.
God chose us in him before the foundation of the world.
God predestined us for adoption as children through Jesus Christ.
Grace was freely given in the Beloved.
In him we have redemption, through his blood, and the forgiveness of sins.

ef-02-graca.context: Paul reminds the readers of where God brought them from. They were dead in transgressions, and the letter shows what God did for them in Christ Jesus.
ef-02-graca.focusQuestion: What changes when you remember that salvation is a gift, not a payment?
ef-02-graca.keywordGloss: God's favor that saves those who could not save themselves, given as a gift.
facts: Being dead, God made us alive together with Christ.
God raised us up and seated us in the heavenly places in Christ.
By grace we are saved through faith, and this is the gift of God.
Salvation is not the result of works, so that no one may boast.
We are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works.
Before, we were without Christ, without hope and without God in the world.

ef-03-igreja.context: At the end of the letter, Paul speaks of a struggle that is not against people. Before naming the pieces of armor, he points to where the strength of those who believe is found.
ef-03-igreja.focusQuestion: Where have you been seeking strength before facing the day?
ef-03-igreja.keywordGloss: What God gives so we can stand firm, starting with truth and righteousness.
facts: Each one will receive from the Lord whatever good they do, whether slave or free.
With the Lord there is no favoritism.
We must be strengthened in the Lord and in the strength of his power.
The armor serves to stand firm against the devil's schemes.
Our struggle is not against flesh and blood.
Standing firm, we must gird ourselves with truth and put on the breastplate of righteousness.

ef-04-desafio.context: This challenge reviews Ephesians, from the blessing in Christ to the armor of God. Paul ties what God has done for us to the firm life we are called to live.
ef-04-desafio.focusQuestion: Which truth from Ephesians do you need to put on today, and not only remember?
ef-04-desafio.keywordGloss: Blessing, salvation and firmness are in Christ, and not in our merit.
facts: God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ.
By grace we are saved through faith, and this is the gift of God.
We are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works.
Before, we were without Christ, without hope and without God in the world.
We must put on the full armor of God in order to stand firm.
Our struggle is not against flesh and blood.
